title: AWS storage services
learningObjective: Identify uses for object storage, S3 storage classes, block storage (EBS, instance store), file services (EFS, FSx), cached hybrid storage (Storage Gateway), lifecycle policies and AWS Backup.
foundation: Amazon S3 stores objects (files) of any size with very high durability, in buckets. Storage classes trade price for access speed.
Amazon EBS gives EC2 instances persistent disks; instance store is temporary disk attached to the host.
Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx provide shared file systems. AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises apps to cloud storage. Lifecycle policies and AWS Backup automate data management.
engineer: S3: designed for 11 nines durability; use cases: backups, data lakes, static websites, media, logs. Storage classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Glacier Deep Archive, Express One Zone. IA and Glacier classes have minimum storage durations and retrieval charges.

Block: Amazon EBS volumes (SSD gp3/io2, HDD st1/sc1) live in one AZ, persist independently of the instance, and support snapshots to S3. Instance store: physically attached, very fast, lost when the instance stops or terminates.
File: Amazon EFS (managed elastic NFS for Linux, Regional across AZs); Amazon FSx (Windows File Server, Lustre for HPC, NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS).
Hybrid: AWS Storage Gateway (S3 File Gateway, FSx File Gateway, Volume Gateway, Tape Gateway) with local cache.

Lifecycle: S3 Lifecycle rules transition objects between classes and expire them (for example logs to Glacier after 90 days, delete after 7 years). AWS Backup: centralised, policy-based backups across EBS, EC2, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3 and more, including cross-Region/cross-account copies.
Other: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers for recovery; Snow Family and DataSync move data.

example.title: Media company storage
body: Raw footage lands in S3 Standard, moves to Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 60 days by lifecycle rule; editors share an FSx for Windows file system; render nodes use instance store scratch space; AWS Backup protects EBS and FSx daily with copies to another Region.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested
portal: S3 > Create bucket > Management > Lifecycle rules.
configuration.cli:
aws s3 mb s3://media-raw-123
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket media-raw-123 --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json
aws backup list-backup-plans

troubleshooting.symptom: Data lost after stopping an instance.

troubleshooting.fix: Use Standard or Intelligent-Tiering for frequently accessed data.

comparisons.difference: S3 ≈ Blob Storage; EBS ≈ Managed Disks; EFS/FSx ≈ Azure Files/NetApp Files; Storage Gateway ≈ File Sync/StorSimple-style; AWS Backup ≈ Azure Backup.

misconceptions.reality: EBS volumes are in one AZ; snapshots go to S3.

misconceptions.myth: S3 One Zone-IA is as resilient as Standard.
misconceptions.reality: It stores data in a single AZ.

architectureDecisions: Use Intelligent-Tiering for unknown access patterns; automate lifecycle and backups.

steps.label: Kinds of data
steps.title: Photos, disks, shared folders, backups
body: Your app stores millions of user photos. Its servers need disks. The office wants a shared drive. Everything needs backups.
AWS has a different storage type for each.

steps.label: S3
steps.title: Photos: object storage in S3
body: Amazon S3 stores objects (files plus metadata) in buckets, accessed over HTTPS. It scales without limit and is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability.
Use it for media, backups, data lakes and static websites.

steps.label: Classes + lifecycle
steps.title: Pay less as data cools down
body: S3 Standard is for frequent access. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA cost less for data you rarely read. Glacier Instant Retrieval, Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive are for archives. Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers automatically.
A lifecycle policy moves or deletes objects by age, for example to Glacier after 90 days and delete after 7 years.

steps.label: Block
steps.title: Server disks: EBS or instance store
body: Amazon EBS volumes are network-attached block disks for EC2. They persist when the instance stops, live in one AZ, and can be snapshotted.
Instance store is a disk physically on the host. It's very fast but temporary: the data is lost when the instance stops or ends.

callout.text: Need data to survive a stop? EBS. Scratch or cache data only? Instance store.

steps.label: File
steps.title: Shared drives: EFS and FSx
body: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system that many Linux instances can mount at once, and it grows automatically.
Amazon FSx provides managed file systems: Windows File Server (SMB), Lustre (high-performance computing), NetApp ONTAP and OpenZFS.

steps.label: Hybrid + backup
steps.title: Bridge on-premises, and back it all up
body: AWS Storage Gateway gives on-premises apps local file, volume or tape interfaces, keeps a cache of hot data on site, and stores the data in AWS.
AWS Backup sets one backup policy (schedule, retention, copies) across EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3 and more.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Object, block, file, hybrid
body: Match the storage type to how the data is used.
